newsitem.title: UK: First Quantum to open Zambia project end-1997.
newsitem.headline: First Quantum to open Zambia project end-1997.

text.p: Canadian mining firm First Quantum Minerals Ltd is ahead of schedule with its copper tailings project in Zambia and plans to advance the start-up date, President Clive Newall said on Tuesday.

The firm, developing the first private mining project in Zambia in 25 years, has also submitted bids for a package of Zambian mines and plants being privatised and will learn the result on April 1, Newall told a presentation in London.
The tailings project, at the site of an abandoned mine in Zambia's copper belt, is now expected to begin production late this year, Newall said.
"It's very well advanced indeed...We are currently four months ahead of schedule on the project," he said.
The Bwana Mkubwa project includes 8.4 million tonnes of tailings with 0.73 percent copper, giving a cash cost of 33 cents per lb ($728 per tonne), Newall said.
Operating profit for the first five-year period is expected to be $133 million based on a copper price of $1.00/lb ($2,205/tonne) and capital expenditure of $27 million, he added.
First Quantum is also undertaking an exploration programme to confirm reserves left when the mine was abandoned and to search for a new orebody.
If an orebody is found that is typical of the region, it could contain 50-300 million tonnes with 1-4 percent grade of copper, First Quantum said in a statement.

Because the firm was the first to be issued a licence under new Zambian mining laws, the company should be well placed among the 33 firms competing for privatised assets of Zambia Consolidated Copper Mines, Newall said.
Preferred bidders will be consulted between now and April 1, when the results will be announced, he added.

First Quantum has bid for the Luanshya mine with 22.1 million tonnes of reserves of 2.32 percent copper plus additional resources. It has also sought the Baluba mine with 31.4 million tonnes of reserves with 2.42 percent copper and 0.17 percent cobalt.
Each mine has a concentrator and Luanshya includes a 48,000 tonne per year smelter.
The firm is also bidding for the Chambishi mine with 33 million tonnes of reserves at 2.55 percent copper, plus a cobalt and acid plant at the site and a precious metals refinery at Ndola.
In addition, First Quantum is involved in joint venture gold exploration projects in Niger, Botswana and Guinea.
